default.notes: Apply for a visa at a Belarusian embassy or consulate before travel; tourist visas generally require a confirmed booking or an invitation.

groups.notes: Visa-free for up to 30 days (capped at 90 days per year) under Belarus's temporary decree for European countries, currently extended — confirm the scheme is still running and which border points accept it before travel.
Visa-free under CIS-era bilateral agreements — typically up to 90 days per year; register with the migration authorities if staying more than 10 days.
Visa-free under a bilateral agreement — typically up to 30 days per visit; confirm the exact allowance with a Belarusian embassy before a long stay.
Visa-free under a bilateral agreement — up to 90 days, counted per year or per 180-day period depending on the agreement; confirm details before a long stay.

Visa-free for up to 30 days only when arriving and departing by air at Minsk National Airport — the waiver does not apply at land borders or on flights to and from Russia; confirm the scheme's current status before booking.

BY.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Belarusian citizens.

RU.notes: Russian citizens enter freely under the Union State — no visas and no border controls on the Belarus–Russia frontier; stays are governed by registration rules rather than a border clock.

RS.notes: Visa-free for up to 30 days per visit under the Belarus–Serbia bilateral agreement.

UA.notes: Formally visa-free for up to 90 days per year under the bilateral agreement, but wartime conditions make direct travel between Ukraine and Belarus effectively impossible — check the practical situation carefully.

IN.notes: An embassy visa is the reliable route; Indian citizens holding a used multiple-entry Schengen, UK or US visa may qualify for the 30-day Minsk airport waiver — verify with a Belarusian embassy first.

XK.notes: Belarus does not recognise Kosovo — Kosovo-issued passports are generally not accepted; contact a Belarusian mission about alternative documents.
